sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: entrance versus exit ramps, left versus right shoulder checks, two-lane versus multi-lane rules, emergency signals and interchange types
Confusable pairs among the highway driving rules, plus continuation facts that complete part C; each block ties to one guide page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A03
An acceleration lane sits at the end of most entrance ramps and is for speeding up, while a deceleration lane sits at the start of most exit ramps and is for slowing down. [A03]
Why it matters: group ramps; confusable acceleration versus deceleration lane; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A03
Entrance ramps and exit ramps are both short ramps that carry traffic in one direction only. [A03]
Why it matters: group ramps; glossary ramp; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A01
The shoulder check flips with the direction of the lane change: before moving out to pass you look over the left shoulder, and before moving back in you look over the right one [A01] [A02].
Why it matters: group passing; confusable left versus right shoulder check; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A01
On a two-lane highway the right lane is the travel lane and the center line may be crossed to pass, while on four or more lanes you keep right except for passing, merging room or a left turn. [A01]
Why it matters: group lane choice; confusable two-lane versus multi-lane; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A03
A white cloth on the antenna and a raised hood are the signals suggested for an emergency stop on the shoulder, together with emergency flashers. [A03]
Why it matters: group emergencies; confusable with the breakdown page list.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A05
The breakdown page adds the side mirror and door handle as places to tie a white cloth, beyond the antenna. [A05]
Why it matters: group emergencies; continuation of the emergency signal list.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A02
After passing a truck, wait until its cab appears in your rearview mirror before returning to the lane, keep your speed, and do not slow down in front of it. [A02]
Why it matters: group trucks; confusable with the general rule of seeing the passed car in the mirror.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A01
The longer you stay in another driver's blind spot while passing, the longer you risk that vehicle moving into yours. [A01]
Why it matters: group passing; continuation of the blind spot rule; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A02
Slow trucks and small underpowered vehicles may lose speed on long or steep climbs and need extra time to get up to speed when they join traffic. [A02]
Why it matters: group slow vehicles; continuation of slow-moving traffic.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A02
Maintain a safe following distance behind the vehicle ahead, as covered in Chapter eight [A02].
Why it matters: group following distance; cross-reference to the following distance rule.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A03
Slowing or changing lanes early may let you avoid stopping entirely, and any stop you do make will be more gradual and safer. [A03]
Why it matters: group stopping; continuation of avoiding panic stops.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A04
The guide pictures four common interchange layouts: cloverleaf, diamond, directional and diverging diamond. [A04]
Why it matters: group interchanges; glossary interchange types; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R13 | anchor: A04
An interchange is where two busy highways meet using entrance and exit ramps, and it can be confusing the first time you use it. [A04]
Why it matters: group interchanges; glossary interchange.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R14 | anchor: A04
Highway hypnosis and plain sleepiness share one fix in the guide: get off the highway rather than risk falling asleep at the wheel. [A04]
Why it matters: group fatigue; confusable hypnosis versus sleepiness; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-R15 | anchor: A01
Many crashes happen because drivers do not give enough attention to driving, so stay alert for unexpected events. [A01]
Why it matters: group attention; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0039]
